- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then decay too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing mean reversion.
- When history shows a sharp upward spike, model reacts with exaggerated peak followed by slow decline.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, often by 1–2 points.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when recent history is volatile or trending up.
- Model fails to adjust downward when true outcome shows a sharp correction after a peak — under-reacts to downward momentum.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overcorrects upward, missing the low zone.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to revert to recent mean quickly, especially after a spike.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5 points for the last 5–10 days if recent history shows downward momentum.
- If model forecast exceeds 75 and true outcome is below 73, reduce forecast by 1–2 points to avoid over-optimism.
